title: Web search without a key and easier local AI setup
summary: I can search the public web without asking you to set up an API key. I also make it easier to get started with local AI and follow what I’m doing in the activity feed.

highlights.title: Web search out of the box
highlights.body: If your model can’t search the web on its own, I can use Keenable to find public sources for you.

highlights.title: Easier local AI setup
highlights.body: I use the graphics memory your computer has available to help choose a model that fits. Inkling 2 Mini replaces Qwen 27B as an option for new local setups. On supported Linux systems with an NVIDIA graphics card, I can download ready-to-run software and skip the build step.

new: I can look for pages published within a date range or read a saved public copy when I have trouble opening the original.
improvements: I show new steps in the activity feed as they happen, with gentle animations that respect your reduced-motion setting.
I keep Grok available if you’ve already set it up. You can also add it when you want it for web or social search.

My FYI notes and READMEs explain why Leon builds its own agent loop and what it means to build personal AI for the long term. The READMEs also show how the project has grown through its GitHub star history.
Leon’s configuration and manifest fields are explained directly in editors that support them.
fixes: You can copy larger images at full resolution. If an image is too large to copy, I point you to the original download.
When you ask for a range of lines in a file, I stop after reading the lines you requested.
I have better safeguards against excessive memory use when streaming OpenAI replies and handling real-time connections.
